html:
The Peoria are one of the peoples of the Illinois Confederation, an alliance of Algonquian-speaking tribes of the upper Mississippi valley. The French explorers Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet met them in 1673 near the Mississippi, and the city of Peoria, on the Illinois River, is named after them.

The Illinois peoples farmed maize in large summer villages and hunted bison on the prairies. In the 1700s wars with the Meskwaki, Sioux and others, together with disease, cut their numbers sharply. As the United States took Illinois, the Peoria gave up their land and moved west to Kansas. There in the 1850s they joined with the Kaskaskia, Wea and Piankashaw, and in 1867 they moved on to Indian Territory. Today they form the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma.
